objective: actual cross-child forced failure produces one terminal event and unchanged return/receipt/cleanup; actual isolated Event Log start delivery distinct from fake, unavailable, or degraded source

seam.executable: the real eliot-host process this integration target launches from the cargo target directory
seam.forced_failure: the SystemService launch shape really enters run_as_scm_service and really calls StartServiceCtrlDispatcherW; the SCM refuses with the documented console case, production records the supported console_fallback boundary, and open_host then refuses the empty registry this isolated run owns, so the child ends at the open_failed boundary with the single console terminal main owns
seam.capture: the child's own stderr tracing sink as the child wrote it, the child's stdout console-protocol frame, the bounded host_start_failure receipt the child wrote into this test's own state root or child temp directory, and a real wevtutil query of the Windows Application log for the delivered Event Log record

main_terminal_drift.note: observe_terminal_error is not a singleton in main.rs: the string occurs at the two real emission sites plus once in the production comment that explains the uncorrelated console terminal. The occurrence count of a callee name is therefore not the terminal-singularity invariant; the exact set of (owning function, typed terminal code) pairs is, and it is what this oracle asserts.

ceiling: The two children prove the forced-failure case across the real Windows SCM service boundary. The Event Log start delivery is executed through the same synchronous production function the bounded producer worker calls (windows_event_log::report_event, reached through report_admitted_event) so the outcome is not a race with the worker's asynchronous shutdown; the child's own asynchronous start delivery cannot be read back deterministically because shutdown_event_log_producer joins no worker and process exit discards queued work, so the child's leg is asserted only as far as its own admission record and that boundary is named here.
